subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should incremental session-memory indexing be pursued as a fresh current-main implementation, rescued from the open candidate PR, or intentionally left as full-entry reindex behavior with existing delta and batching controls?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, overlap semantics, and whether the conflicting open candidate branch is still worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade, overlap, compaction, and real-behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the candidate PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or an owner to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before further review.

options.title: Keep full-entry consistency
options.body: Close or de-scope incremental indexing only if maintainers prefer full-entry consistency plus existing delta/batch controls over the added complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade, overlap, compaction, and real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent transcript corpus and session identity work makes this the best available owner for the design choice.
